newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-BBC and ICL to set up Internet service.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BBC and ICL to set up Internet service.

text.p: The British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) on Thursday unveiled an alliance with Japanese-controlled information technology company ICL to develop a commercial online Internet service.
The venture, which has the working title BBC Online, will provide a BBC-branded web service and is targeted for launch on the global computer network in early 1997.
It will be built around popular BBC radio and television programmes and magazines and will cover news, sport, information and entertainment.

"This will play an absolutely vital role in stimulating consumer acceptance (of the Internet) and moving forward to greater interactivity," BBC Worldwide chief executive Bob Phillis told a news conference.
The project between BBC Worldwide, the corporation's commercial arm, and ICL, controlled by Japan's giant Fujitsu Ltd, will initially run until the end of 1999.
ICL chief executive Keith Todd said his company was investing "many millions of pounds" in the venture.
ICL is funding the venture as BBC Online is subject to regulations that ensure no public money is used to finance any of BBC Worldwide's commercial ventures.
The BBC will supply the creative content while ICL will be responsible for providing the systems integration services, as well as technical expertise.

The project aims to provide fast and simple Internet access through a BBC-branded software package and access service. Access will also be available through managed services such as CompuServe and America Online AMER.O.
Todd said the content would initIally be heavily based on text and graphics, but Phillis said the aim was to add audio and visual services as technology advanced.

Phillis said the service would at first be tailored for a British audience but he expected it eventually to be marketed internationally. There are plans to carry advertising and charge a subscription for premium services.
The deal is part of the BBC's efforts to expand its commercial activities and lessen its dependence on the licence fee, a tax which must be paid by anyone with a television set.
Net benefit from commercial ventures was 77 million pounds in 1995/96, a sum dwarfed by the 1.8 billion pounds raised by the licence fee charged to all Britons with a television.

BBC director-general John Birt last month called for an above inflation hike in the annual licence fee, which currently stands at 89.50 pounds ($140) for a colour service. But his call met with a frosty response from politicians from Britain's two main parties.
The BBC is also in joint venture talks with rival pay television groups BSkyB and Flextech about the launch of new subscription channels based on BBC programming. ($1=.6412 Pound)
